key: folk:crocodile:The Pyretooth|theropod|volcano|ash|Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago|

narrator.persona: a calm, warm storyteller, like a nature documentary narrator who is quietly afraid

sentences.text: For millions of years the tyrant lizard was the undisputed apex predator of this valley and nothing dared hunt it.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Herds of long-necked giants and flying reptiles kept far away from the king while his deafening thunder-roar shook the trees.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: A volcano that had slept for ages began to violently shake until the dark ground cracked open and the animals fell completely silent.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: It finally erupted with ash and fire and thunder, sending every living creature running, and for the first time even the king fled.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: In the molten crater something vast moved as heat and choking ash gathered into a towering body born straight from the flames with glowing cracks across its hide.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: It opened its burning eyes and took its first heavy breath, already much bigger than the king while the earth groaned beneath its claws.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The old king stepped forward with fierce pride to challenge the usurper, but one sudden strike ended his ancient reign in an instant.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Now the valley belongs to a new and terrifying master, but what happens when this fire-born monster finally leaves its home?
sentences.speaker: narrator
